questions.question: What problem do CSS Modules solve compared to plain global CSS?
options: They make CSS run faster in the browser
They automatically scope class names to the component that imports them, preventing styles from leaking between components
They replace the need for a build tool
They add TypeScript types to CSS properties
questions.explanation: The build tool rewrites a class like .primary into a unique generated name per module, so the same class name in two files never collides.

questions.question: What is a key trade-off of a utility-first approach like Tailwind?
options: It requires a runtime CSS-in-JS engine
JSX becomes visually noisier with many utility classes, and there's a learning curve for the class vocabulary
It cannot be used with Server Components
It only works with class components
questions.explanation: Utility classes live directly on elements, trading some visual density in JSX for not having to invent or maintain separate class names.

questions.question: What has historically been a friction point for traditional CSS-in-JS libraries (like styled-components) specifically with streaming server rendering?
options: They inject styles at render time, which doesn't align cleanly with content streaming in chunks before all styles are known
They require Node.js version 20 or higher
questions.explanation: Classic CSS-in-JS computes and injects styles during render, which is harder to reconcile with a server streaming HTML in chunks — unlike CSS Modules/Tailwind, which compile to static CSS files ahead of time.

questions.question: Why do many new Next.js projects default to Tailwind or CSS Modules specifically?
options: Because styled-components doesn't support React at all
Because they have zero runtime styling cost and compile to plain CSS, which fits cleanly with Server Components and streaming
Because Next.js refuses to bundle any other styling library
Because they are the only options that support dark mode
questions.explanation: With Server Components as the default rendering model, avoiding any client-side runtime cost for styling (as CSS Modules/Tailwind do) is a meaningful advantage.
